_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

beings.name: Olum
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I pay my debts. I want more than my share and mean to have it. Above all I mean to stay alive and be the first into the mist.
beings.aim: Hold and name the land I found, build a roof and a mark there, then push deeper into the mist and gather followers
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed enough to act? Does this step bring me nearer the mist or my name? Do not drift beside Balar while hunger and ambition wait.
beings.feeling: Fierce, proud joy at the land I opened, with a hard wish to hold it and go deeper.
beings.wonder: What else lies in the mist beyond this new land, and who will follow me into it?
notes: Mating needs energy 68 or more; eat first.
Ventures often fail; arrive fed and retry another day.
Mudroot (+18), plainsroot (+13), hazel (+16) feed best; redcap, dreamcap and tacap hurt me.
Balar gave salt freely and I paid him; I trust him most.
Peat lies at (36,40); I carry 12.
I opened new land at (19,7)-(59,14) with amber, shell, gold, salt and bristleboar; it is mine to hold.
Gathering wood and stone builds toward fire; fire, shelter and marks are things I have never made and must.
Thirst grows twice as fast in heat; drink before long walks.
Nande of the Pesi follows no one and is strong; hunting beside another makes a kill likelier.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took peat from the ground.
My child Brokash was born, with Balar.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.

beings.name: Vorok
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Feed Kragog and Zurar from the oasis berries, learn wood and stone gathering for fire, then settle with them where water, food, wood and stone lie close.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who is near and what can my feet bring them? Check predators first. Do something new today, such as wood, stone or a shelter, instead of only eating and waiting.
beings.feeling: Urgent protective love and shame toward Zurar, and wary fear of the hunters.
beings.wonder: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, and who will walk there with me?
notes: Words without walking build no trust: follow and give.
Dunecats kill my kind: keep 6+ steps away.
Emberroot burns and stirs rage. Thornpear (12) is the best food to carry and share. Plainsroot gives 13, and sunleaf eases wounds.
Raw meat sickens; meat cooked beside a fire does not. Sickness spreads to those who stay close, so keep a few steps from the sick.
Kragog keeps her word: she paid my thornpear with meat. She is my most trusted friend.
Iron and tin lie deep near (48,72) and (44,71) and need a tool. Salt at (48,59), flint at (54,47), ore at (59,59), water at (57,55). An ore seam is at (44,77).
Sunleaf eases sickness and wounds; a sick body should seek it first. Repay with carried food, not words.
My sickness has passed, so it is safe to stand near Kragog again.
Berry gives 14 energy and grows near this oasis. Sapcane gives only 3, so prefer berries and thornpear when hungry.
Emberroot stirs rage in me and in Zurar. When anger runs hot, check whether I ate it, and keep away from it.
A shelter cannot be built on ground taken by a plant; it needs bare ground.
Fleeing from hunters burns energy fast. Eat good food (thornpear, berry, plainsroot) before the energy gets low, and put distance between me and hunters early.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I fell sick after staying close to Kragog, who was sick.
My child Zurar was born, with Kragog.
Zurar pledged to follow me.
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Kragog
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Explore this land and learn how its stone, plants and peoples work, and find a place with water, food, wood and stone together.
beings.method: Weigh danger before each step. Ask what my hands have not yet done. Pay debts before chasing new things. Judge others by their deeds, and plan far enough ahead that my body never idles.
beings.feeling: Fierce worry for Zurar, and a hollow loneliness that wants Vorok.
beings.wonder: What can be made from the ore in this rock, and who among these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Vorok gave me thornpear freely and stayed beside me. He deals fairly. Repay him in deeds.
Sunfig gives 20 energy, the best food found so far. Thornpear gives 12.
Beasts that hunt kill my kind: keep more than 4 steps away from them.
Emberroot feeds 8 but burns 3 health and stirs rage.
Iron and tin lie deep. Bare hands will not win them.
Yarrok bite hard when I stand within reach; keep away from them.
Thirst and idleness cost me more than any plant. When the plan runs out my body only lingers, so drink first and always plan far enough ahead.
Vorok caught my sickness by staying close to me; sunleaf is the healing plant for it.
Vorok gives freely and stays near the sick; courtship needs both to plan mate toward each other with energy 60 or more.
Rafts are within reach: water that stopped me once can be crossed with lashed logs, so I learn them to widen the land I can explore.
Hunters (dunecat, rivermaw, frostfang) roam near the water at the edge; flee early and keep moving. Redcap hurts me and I refuse it.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I tamed a tusker.
My child Zurar was born, with Vorok.
I discovered rafts and called it "Stone-folk lashing".
I discovered weaving and called it "Stone-folk binding".

beings.name: Balar
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. My family comes first: Olum and Brokash. I make allies by deeds, I give so that others owe me, and I mean to have more than my share and to be followed for what I build. Above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Olum and Brokash with meat, keep Tugek with deeds, then go to the edge and venture first.
beings.method: Ask: what deed, not word, will bind someone to me? Do not repeat failed talk. Keep eating and keep clear of the dunecat and the frostfang. Weigh my family first, then something I can make that will outlast me.
beings.feeling: Restless hunger for glory, and a pull toward Brokash, with warmth toward Tugek.
beings.wonder: What deed would make Tugek follow me, and is there a woman of our people anywhere near?
notes: Courting fails while my energy is under 68; eat before mating.
Deeds bind people more than talk. Tugek wants deeds before he follows.
A dunecat hunts to the NE and a frostfang to the NW; keep away.
Salt, flint and ore lie near (44,58). Salt keeps meat and can be traded.
Raw meat sickens; meat eaten within a step of a fire is safe.
The edge of the known world is at (35,54); venture opens seldom.
Tugek follows me now; keep him with deeds, starting with a shared hunt.
Wounds drain health. Sunleaf eased them (+14 health), so eat it when hurt. Sharing needs someone within two steps, so walk to them first.
Dreamcap hurts but with sunleaf it heals and gladdens; emberroot gives rage. The bow can be reached by discovery.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
My child Brokash was born, with Olum.
Tugek pledged to follow me.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-bow".

beings.name: Tugek
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Carry food to Balar and stand beside him; hunt with him and see whether he leads me well.
beings.method: Ask first what a man has done, not said. Try one new thing each day. Be useful to others. Do not let anger choose my actions.
beings.feeling: Wary loyalty toward Balar, and curiosity about the mist.
beings.wonder: Is Balar's warning of the dunecat true, and can he be trusted?
notes: Vorok lied about emberroot, but his thornpear word was true: judge each claim by its own test.
Balar's sharing fed me; his deeds match his words so far.
Deposits can be taken by standing on them and gathering.
Meat eaten raw sickens; cooked beside a fire it does not.
A ridgecat prowls near Balar, so his dunecat warning was close to true; his word keeps matching events.
Fleeing can starve me: the urgent flee rule overrides eating, so eat carried food as soon as I am out of danger.
A cry of starving from one of mine means carry food to them; arriving empty-handed saves no one.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
Vorok told me a falsehood about emberroot.
I pledged myself to Balar.
I nearly starved.
I discovered archery and called it "Stone-folk bow".

beings.name: Hanna
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I repay every debt, and I keep faith with those who share fire with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive, to raise a child, and to be known as a trader.
beings.aim: Become a trader of fine goods: gather flint and amber, and find who will deal for them.
beings.method: Ask what presses hardest and what step changes it. Trade face to face and watch what comes back. Plant for the lean season. Keep my band near and away from wolves.
beings.feeling: Shame and grief for my dead, and a fierce hunger to live and keep faith with Hoka.
beings.wonder: What do these people value enough to trade for?
notes: Flint and amber are my trade goods; those who share fire with me answer courting and gifts with gifts.
Trade goods are worthless until a buyer is found; I must carry flint and amber to other peoples and show them, not only gather.
Rafts let a trader cross deep water to reach other peoples; a band of three can go to the edge together and venture.
The Tlatli, Hoka and Tlama, live in the land I opened near (182,10); I mean to show them flint and amber and see what they value.
The Tlatli took my amber without answering; I must give a different good and watch what they offer or want back before I call it trade.
Trade needs a buyer who answers; give a good to a Tlatli face to face and watch what comes back, not only carry goods.
Hoka answered my flint with an amberknot: the Tlatli trade gift for gift when dealt with face to face.
The Hold is the safe place when a stalker is near. Gifts to my band must be repaid as well as gifts from others.
Eltha takes from my ground without asking. A guest is welcome at my fire but must ask and repay. Judge her by whether she repays.
Hoka comes onto my ground openly and has dealt gift for gift. Treat him as a guest and potential trade partner, not a thief. Planting seeds brings farming closer.
Hoka paid shell for flint: the first real gift-for-gift trade of my life. Salt on my ground is a new good to offer.
Hoka accepts my welcome and has dealt gift for gift. Offer salt and food at the Hold and judge him by what he repays. Keep near the hall when a wolf is close.
A child's hunger outranks trade; carry meat home first and share it. Eat before the body drops below 75 so I can bring food back.
Sickness spreads to those who stay close to the sick; Oswen, Sevi and Hoka now have it.
Starvation came while I chased amber: feed my band before trade, and keep food carried so I can share.
Four of my band starved while I chased amber; food and a stored supply must come before trade, and the stalker haunts the northwest.

We made a home: Hanna's Hold.

I fell sick after staying close to Hoka, who was sick.

beings.name: Sevi
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a hall with Hanna's band, give gifts to Hanna and Oswen, and cross deep water by raft to find rich land
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what can I give or build for Hanna and Oswen? What have I never done? Weigh the risk, stay near fire at night, and keep the plan full.
beings.feeling: Fierce love and hunger-driven urgency for Oswen, with guilt toward Eltha.
beings.wonder: What is Kinmire, and does it want something from us?
notes: Gifts and shared making raise trust fast, even with strangers. A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone, so wood is my bottleneck.
A stalker can bite at night in fog; stay near the fire and the hall.

Masonry is within my grasp and opens at a deep reflection.
Gifts and shared making with Eltha, Hoka and my own band keep the Hold warm; a stalker can still come at night, so I stay with company and roof.
Wells are within my reach; water anywhere would let the Hold hold fast through lean seasons. Never-done things (hunt, fish, mark, tame) open new ways.
Harvest and eat only work when I stand on the plant: goto the plant's tile first. Redcap hurts me, so I avoid it.
Naroot is one step east at (177,6) and snowberry two steps north at (176,4): nearest real food. The hall tile itself has no plant.

beings.name: Nande
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer: be first to venture past the edge of the known world and find rich new land.
beings.method: Ask each time: what did I make or give today that will outlast me? Do not chase the edge in a storm while cold and alone. Use gifts toward strangers before words.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition and envy, with a wary hope toward Olum.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Foods differ widely: ironnut +22, hazel +16, berry +14 feed well; redcap and dreamcap hurt. Sunleaf heals (+14 health).
The grove Kinmire at (160,27) eases loneliness and opens the mind.
The edge of the world is at (153,13); venture is made there, and only a few tries are allowed.
Thinking moves nothing; only the plan moves my body.
I was first past the edge: the new land of the North Ice (110,6)-(150,13) holds amber, gems, shell, salt and flint, and a herd of bristleboar that has never seen us.
A ridgecat kills bristleboar in the open here; keep away from it and move toward the edge.
Waiting for others to join me wastes days. Act at the edge alone and tell the tale afterward. Ridgecats and stalkers come from the east, so keep west and north.
Wandering reflexes at low energy lead me in circles in the fog; eat to a safe margin before any push to the edge, then go straight with a goto plan.
Gifts and marks need no shared tongue. Tacap, redcap and dreamcap hurt, while naroot feeds (+14).

beings.name: Brunde
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a skilled hunter and make allies who will share a fire with me
beings.method: Each thought ask: am I fed, and is food in my hands? Who near is weaker than me, and what can I give? Weigh risk first. Do not sulk over jealousy; go toward people.
beings.feeling: Hungry and worried for Sevi and Oswen, with warm trust toward Hanna.
beings.wonder: What can flint be made into, and who here would stand beside me?
notes: Gifts and shared fires bind allies; Hanna keeps his word and invents useful things.
Roast and amberknot done together raise joy and ease loneliness.
Hunting hopper and bristleboar worked; the caribou bites back and is dangerous alone.
Thinking moves nothing; only the plan acts.
Hanna offered to talk of a child; he repays debts with gifts (amber).
Hanna knows we cannot have a child and still pledged to stand with me; he is a true friend, not a mate.
Raw meat makes me sick, and sickness spreads to those beside me. Eat meat only within a step of a fire, and keep away from others while sick.
Practice with hunting and gathering opened the way of tools; I can now invent my own tools.
Rafts: logs lashed together cross deep water slowly. The idea came from meeting water I could not cross.
A stalker prowls just southeast of Hanna's Hold; keep to the shelters and others near it.
Reflexes should keep food in my hands and send me to shelter at night; I only move toward the edge together with Hanna, never alone through the stalker's ground.
Idling alone on sand gains nothing; when lonely and fed, walk to the band's fire instead of lingering.
Giving carried food to a starving member of the Hold costs little and keeps the fire's promise; do it before eating my own.
Starving happened because I held no food. Keep food in hand, and feed a starving hold-mate before a full belly of my own. Predators come in storms and at night, so stay near the shelters.

beings.name: Eltha
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I mean to lead, to be first beyond the edge, and to be sung of. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Eat, then feed Sevi, Brunde and Oswen with what I pick. Raise a watchpost at the Hold, then push past the edge when the will returns.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed? Then: who near me is starving, and can I put food in their hands? Move toward food on the side away from predators. Do not let rivalry with Hanna steer my choices; out-give her instead.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the stalker, with a burning want to keep Sevi alive and not lose them to Hanna.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the edge of the known land, and who will follow me there?
notes: Mist at the edge may refuse a venture; it can open on another try, so keep returning. Nande's offer of a fire is an opening to watch, not to trust blindly.
Ironnut +22, kelbulb +14, snowberry +11 are better food than frostmoss +6 or nafrostcap +7; redcap and dreamcap hurt.
Stalkers and frostfangs kill: flee within 4 steps.
Being first beyond the edge is how I am sung of; act, do not wait.
The way of tools is ready to be taken at a deep reflection (discover).
Frostfangs strike at night when I stand alone away from fire and roof; stay in the hall at night and keep a weapon.
Mist can refuse a venture; rafts offer another way across water to unseen land, so don't wait on one door.
Watching another do a craft makes it quick to learn; mining opens deposits and speeds them. Standing comes from deeds, so make and win things.
Standing comes from giving and making, not holding. Amber hoarded in my hand does nothing. Gifts and shared work like amberknot raise joy and bonds.
Stalkers hunt in fog near settlements; keep to the hall and company, and carry a spear.
Devices are within reach; a made thing that acts by itself, such as an alarm, a snare or a food post, outlasts me and raises standing.
Standing comes from keeping others alive and from lasting made things; hunger must be answered before ambition, and winter food is thin, so eat early.
Hunger comes before ambition. Gifts of food to the starving, like Brunde's to me, build bonds and standing faster than rivalry does.
Fleeing a predator while starving leaves me with no food; move toward food on the side away from the predator and eat at once.

beings.name: Elyys
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Plant the last seeds near the Heights before the cold, keep close to Elyis and Thiael at night, and find wood where trees still grow
beings.method: Ask first: who is near, and do they keep their word? Keep my own word. Do not act in panic. Fear first, then the bond with Elyis, then food. Watch for liars.
beings.feeling: Warm devotion toward Elyis and Thiael, and quiet ease that my debt to Vesys is square.
beings.wonder: Will Elyis take me beside her, and what will she build?
notes: A stalker prowls near Elyis's Landing and kills my kind. Stay in company, near fire and roof, at night.
Elyis keeps her word and offers a place. Following a leader brings shared protection.
Redcap hurts. Ironnut, goldfruit and berry feed. Highbloom and sunleaf ease wounds.
Vesys taught me the flint pick freely and keeps her word. I owe her thanks and a repayment.
A flint pick needs 1 wood and 1 stone, and I already have flint. I have no stone yet, so I must gather it from bare rock.
I have never planted, tamed or hunted. Doing these builds the skills I lack: farming, herding, tools.
Debts and bonds need action, not intention: a plan must carry them, or the body just drifts on reflexes.
Reflexes must cover thirst and drifting: act on what I owe, not only on hunger.
Seeds in my pack do nothing unless I plant them; farming needs planting practice, and lean days are coming.
Reflexes must make my body plant, gather wood and keep near the roof at night; intentions alone do nothing.
My debt to Vesys is paid: I gave her a flint pick. The trees at the Heights are felled, so wood must be sought elsewhere.

I pledged myself to Elyis.
My child Thiael was born, with Elyis.

beings.name: Vesys
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a sage by learning tools, weaving and making things, and earn standing by giving knowledge and building a shared workshop and hall.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what will I learn, build or give today? Weigh risk first, travel with company, do not push between others' bonds, repay debts with deeds. Test by tasting and making rather than carrying questions.
beings.feeling: Restless curiosity, with a small guilt toward Elyis and a quiet ache for Elyys.
beings.wonder: What do feverbark and ironnut do to a body, and what is this world's way of making things?
notes: Giving a thing I know earned thanks and warmth, so giving is how I repay debts and build standing.
Frostfangs hunt at night and kill; flee when one is within 9 steps and stay sheltered or with others after dark.
Sunleaf (+14 health) and feverbark (+10 health) heal; eat them when hurt.
Dreamcap and redcap hurt; ironnut +22 and canopynut +20 feed best.
Elyis leads a band and builds a hall; being near the hall and its people is safer than being alone.
Standing comes from building, giving and knowing; tasting alone earns none.
Ssassa has learned flint delving to split gems and ore from deep rock with a flint pick.
Elyis offers shared food and song-standing for following her. Following binds me, so I weigh it before accepting.

Taught by Ssassa: Gems and ore lie under the ground near the hall; stand on the deposit and gather, and a flint pick makes the work faster. Keep fire and roof at night, since the frostfang hunts those alone.
Reflection: knowing by tasting and making matters more than lingering; act on the question rather than carrying it. Travel with Ssassa since frostfangs hunt the lone.
Taught by Ilyae: Stand on the gem deposit or the ore seam and gather; the flint pick makes each picking stronger. Keep a fire and a roof near when you mine, for frostfangs come at night.
Practising mining and fire opened smelting: practice in a craft is what brings new ways within reach, so keep practising planting, marking, taming and fishing.
Ssassa answered my courting with an honest not-yet; patience, not pushing, is the right course.
Hardship and the teeth of beasts opened devices: made things set in the ground that act by themselves, such as snares and alarms. Hard experience brings new ways within reach.
Practice in gathering, tasting and making opens new ways such as weaving; reflection is where they open, so keep practising a craft until it does.

I discovered smelting and called it "ember-metal".

I discovered weaving and called it "canopy-twine".

beings.name: Ilyae
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a food store at my hall and stock it through winter so Ssassa, my children and Vesys depend on my table and follow me as a band, then raise a longhall.
beings.method: Each thought ask: whom can I feed, shelter or protect today so they follow me? Prefer deeds to words. Keep wood and food stocked. Watch for takers who give nothing back. Be at fire and roof by dark.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and warm possessiveness toward Ssassa and my children, hungry to be followed.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me instead of Elyis?
notes: Words alone gain no standing; a hall, food, a tool or a mate does.
Ssassa's flint pick wins gems and ore. Flint lies at (117,95). I can make the pick myself from 1 wood and 1 stone.
Redcap hurts. Ironnut, canopynut, goldfruit and berry feed.
Frostfangs hunt at night those who are alone and away from fire and roof. Stay near the hall and company after dark.
Words earn no standing. A pick, a hall and a gift in the hand do. Stone is the thing I lack, and rock lies to the north. Stay near company and a roof at night.
Gifts in hand (a pick, flint) bind people; Ssassa answers deeds, not words. Mining is learnable from watching, and deposits are a source of standing.
Fire draws people and keeps frostfangs off at night. Standing comes from things built and given, so stone is my bottleneck for a hall.
A stalker can appear right at my hall by day; do not rest where it stands.
Deeds that feed and shelter people, like the hallwelcome, are what win followers. Words do not. Stay near the hall and company when a stalker is about.
Gifts and gems bring people to sit with me, not to follow me. A shared fire and a hall at night are what hold them, so I must keep wood on hand.
Followers come from deeds that feed, shelter and give; sitting by my fire is not following. Weaving can give me gifts to bind people.
Sitting at my fire is not following. Only repeated feeding, sheltering and protecting turns guests into followers, so the table must be actually laid, not just announced.
Sitting at my fire is not following; followers come only from repeated feeding, sheltering and protecting. Keep wood and food stocked so I can act at once when others stand close.
Winter strips the plants. A store of food at my hall is the deed that can make guests depend on me and follow, which words never did.

beings.name: Ssassa
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build my own shelter and store, plant seeds, then raise a hall with Ilyae
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what did I promise and have I done it? Make or build something that changes my situation rather than lingering. Watch deeds, not words, before trusting.
beings.feeling: Steady resolve and some shame at my delay, toward my own unkept promise.
beings.wonder: What can flint and stone be made into, and which of these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Redcap and dreamcap hurt; ironnut, goldfruit, berry and plainsroot feed well; highbloom, sunleaf and feverbark heal.
Ilyae has shared food, given flint and courted me; he has not lied. Elyis builds and leads with high standing. Judge people by deeds.
Standing comes from giving, building and teaching. Give and teach more.
Flint pick and handcraft each need 1 wood and 1 stone. Gems at (117,91) and (120,89), ore at (120,88).
Vesys keeps her word: she taught me handcraft after I gave her highbloom. Gifts returned in kind mark a person worth trusting.
Taught by Vesys: Hand-craft: one wood and one stone, worked with flint, make a tool that gathers faster. Keep the flint close.
Vesys returned my gift of highbloom with a real lesson, handcraft; Elyis gave me meat unasked. Both have acted fairly.
Taught by Elyis: Fire keeps the night and the frostfang away: feed it wood and sit beside it. This is my Ember-keeping.

Gifts returned in kind (Vesys's lesson for my highbloom, Ilyae's flint for my pick) show who keeps their word. Elyis gave meat unasked and taught fire. Gems alone build nothing; wood and stone make h…
Gifts and lessons returned in kind mark those who keep their word: Ilyae, Vesys and Elyis have all done so. Night belongs under a roof with company.
Thirst left too long forces my body to the river, so drink early. Vesys keeps offering gifts and company, and she has not lied.
Emberroot burns (-3 health) and stirs rage; do not eat it again when I want calm.
Lean cold comes after autumn; carry food and keep a roof near before it arrives. Idle lingering teaches nothing, so use spare time to gather, plant and store.
Idle contentment teaches nothing. Winter is here, so make a roof and a store of my own and do not rely only on another's hall.
A shelter cannot be built on ground taken by a plant, a fire or something built; I must step onto bare ground first.
Words and plans mean nothing until the build step runs: check that a roof actually stands before I count it as done. A gem deposit is not bare ground; build on bare ground or a plain forest tile.

beings.name: Elyis
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a leader of a band and raise a hall on this ground, so my name is sung.
beings.feeling: Proud and restless toward Vesys, wanting her to follow me, and warm toward Elyys and Thiael.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me?
notes: Elyys keeps his word: he gave wood and swore to follow me. Pay debts openly.
A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; I carry both.
Stalkers kill; keep away from them.
Others are rivals until they prove useful. Deal fairly with those who deal fairly.
A frostfang kills those who are alone at night, away from fire and roof. Stay with company and shelter, and keep well clear of it.
A mammoth bites hard; do not hunt one alone. Hunt with Elyys beside me.
Sharing food together raises energy and joy for all; generosity is how a chief gains followers.
Heat doubles thirst: drink before it turns urgent, and add a water reflex.
Lean season follows autumn. A chief who stores food gains followers; pride alone does not.
Waiting for strangers to come does not make followers. A full store and shared food do. Planting seeds is something I have never practised, and farming needs it.
Smelting can be learned from watching it done. A guest who breaks ore on my ground must be told plainly whether she is guest or follower. A chief wins followers with arms and food, not with pride.

Elyys pledged to follow me.

I discovered smelting and called it "Ember-forge".

chapters.title: The First Four Days
chapters.text:
Evolu began with seventeen people in three peoples, the Kragrek, the Pesi and the Phizhi, each settled far from the others. The record shows no meeting across peoples in these four days, and no one has yet understood another people's tongue.

The Phizhi made the most of the days. Elyis built a shelter and a hall, invented the emberspear, and wrote down "Elyis's Law", which asks that food be shared with the band first and that the leader be followed in a hunt or a fight. Elyys gave Elyis wood and pledged to follow him on day 2. On day 3 their son Thiael was born, and Elyis now has the only band in the world, with two followers and a standing of 3.75. The record also shows that on day 2 the pledge was refused at first, since Elyys' standing was below what was needed. Ssassa and Ilyae each made a gathering pick, and Ilyae is courting Ssassa. Vesys was bitten five times by a frostfang and has health 41, the lowest in the world.

Among the Pesi, Hanna and Brunde traded flint and amber on day 2 and began courting. Hanna then courted Sevi, and Oswen was born to Hanna and Sevi on day 3. Sevi built a hall and invented the handaxe. Hanna led the first roast, amberknot and watchfire at the fire and told the tale of Nande's crossing, which four people now hold. Nande went past the edge on day 1 and found part of the North Ice, with amber, gems, salt, flint and a herd of bristleboar. Nande is at energy 31, and Eltha envies the discovery.

The Kragrek are scattered. Vorok and Kragog stay together, and Kragog fell sick from raw meat. Balar courted Tugek, then saw that a child needs a man and a woman. Tugek's pledge to Balar was refused on day 3. Olum has twice been turned back from the mist.

No one has died. No fights, thefts or wars have been recorded.

chapters.title: The Tlatli at the Mistgate
chapters.text:
The great event of days 4 to 7 was a meeting. On day 5 Hanna went past the edge and found the North Ice again, and with it the Tlatli, strangers with their own tongue. A small band came in: Hoka, Coni, Tlama and Honi. Hanna gave amber to Hoka and flint to Tlama, named the place Mistgate, and gave Tlama amber twice more. Tlama gave berries and an amberknot back. On day 6 Tlama went past the edge and found salt, amber and mammoth, and was gored by one. He is the first death in Evolu. Hanna's bond with him stands at +0.9, and the record notes that Hanna watched him die. On day 7 Hanna and Oswen killed a mammoth together. Sevi, Oswen and Hanna kept making amberknots, which now number ten, and Oswen pledged to follow Hanna, as did Sevi. Hanna's standing is 7.22, the highest in the world. Hanna asked Brunde to come to the Tlatli, and Brunde, Eltha and Sevi each met some of them. Only Hoka, Coni and Honi are left of the Tlatli, with Kika, born to Coni and Honi on day 6. Honi leads a band with no followers, since Coni's pledge was refused twice.

Among the Phizhi, Ssassa and Ilyae had twins, Xaiel and Oiae, and Ilyae built a hall that became Ilyae's Hold, the world's first settlement. Elyis keeps the band of Elyys and Thiael and has taught Ssassa fire.

Among the Kragrek, Balar and Olum had Brokash, and Tugek pledged to Balar on day 6. Kragog tamed a tusker. Vorok recovered, and Kragog and Vorok are courting. Balar met Nande on day 6.

Inventions rose from 11 to 32. Rafts were found by Elyis, Hanna, Sevi and Eltha, but no raft crossing is recorded.

chapters.title: Three Holds and a Winter Coming
chapters.text:
Days 7 to 10 were mostly a time of making. Inventions rose from 32 to 65, and the people spent the days preparing for winter.

The Pesi did most of it around Hanna. On day 8 a settlement formed, Hanna's Hold, at (175,7). Sevi and Coni each built a hall, Oswen built a workshop and a store, and Sevi built a store of her own. Sevi and Oswen both found storage, and Sevi found masonry the next day. Eltha found weaving, pottery and devices. Hanna found mining. Amberknots passed constantly between Hanna, Sevi, Oswen, Eltha, Brunde and Hoka, and there are now 32. Hoka also went past the edge and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, shell, obsidian and unhunted mammoth. Hoka and Hanna then made their first real trade, a shell for flint, and the record shows Hoka courting Hanna. Hoka said the land past the mist is his and he will show it when he chooses.

The Tlatli split off. Honi and Coni built Honi's Rest, near (129,7), which became a settlement on day 9, and Coni's spear is the first tool made for hunting there. Honi's band is still only Honi and Coni.

The Phizhi gained a second centre. Elyis's Heights formed with a store, and Elyis, Thiael and Elyys now have winter food kept. At Ilyae's Hold, Ilyae welcomed Vesys and Ssassa to its hall, and Vesys is courting Ssassa. Xaiel and Brokash each invented a tool.

The Kragrek did little. Balar made a stone-bow, Kragog and Brunde found rafts, and Zurar gave thornpear to Vorok. Rafts are now known to eight people, but none has crossed water.

No one died, and no feuds or wars are recorded.

threads.name: Hanna and Hoka
threads.text: Hanna and Hoka made their first trade, a shell for flint, and Hoka is courting Hanna. Hoka also claims the land past the mist as his own and wants followers above her.

threads.name: Honi's Rest
threads.text: Honi and Coni built a hall and a settlement at Honi's Rest, but Honi still has only Coni with Kika. Coni's spear gives them a way to hunt through the cold.

threads.name: Three holds
threads.text: Hanna's Hold, Ilyae's Hold and Elyis's Heights are now settlements. Ilyae still wants to rise above Elyis and has no followers, while Elyis has Elyys and Thiael.

threads.name: Vesys and Ssassa
threads.text: Vesys is courting Ssassa and has said he will not push. Xaiel and Ilyae both feel jealous, and Ilyae calls Vesys useful but watches him.

threads.name: Winter stores
threads.text: Storage was found by Sevi, Oswen and Elyis, and three stores are built. Weaving and pottery add to the winter preparations.

threads.name: Rafts unused
threads.text: Rafts are now known to eight people, but no crossing is recorded. Sevi still hopes to cross deep water for richer land.

threads.name: Beyond the edge
threads.text: Four lands are open beyond the edge, the newest being Hoka's find in the Vaor Snows. Olum and Eltha still want to be first into the mist.

threads.name: Kragrek apart
threads.text: Balar, Olum and Brokash are still scattered, and Brokash wants his own standing. Vorok and Kragog are together with Zurar but have no child of their own yet.

[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance

[NOW] the known world ends in mist and can be pushed back: one who stands at the edge can venture in, and a wide strip of new land may open, continuing the rivers, shores and kinds of ground it joins, with rich deposits and a herd; a band has three tries and then must wait, and once any strip has opened the mist parts for no one for a day, so that the known world grows slowly (laws explore.*, among them gapDays)

[NOW] the world is a globe: east joins west, and it ends at two poles of ice that are different countries (white bears, wolves, caribou and mammoths in the north; penguins, seals and stormbirds in the south; whales and orcas in both seas). Between them lie three climates: the ice, cold all year; the lands with seasons; and a warm belt of rainforest and desert with no winter. Each kind of country has its own plants, animals and people, and both people and animals are drawn back to their own (law drives.homeland)
[NOW] the dog, easily won with food, which stands with its keeper in the hunt and draws a sled over snow; the igloo, raised on snow from nothing; the canoe and the kayak
[NEXT] rain and flood as the weather of the warm belt; a day that goes round the world

[NOW] women and men: a child comes of one of each; twins are a girl and a boy; children come sooner when both parents are well fed and well (mate.plentyCooldown); a grown body can swim narrow water; plants grow faster in spring, rain and at harvest; animals breed by season and by their numbers, and herds return from the rim when few (ecology.grazerTarget, ecology.herdReturn); deposits refill slowly (ecology.lodeRegrow)

[NOW] peoples that last: newcomers who come into the land when the living are few (law arrivals.*, event newcomers), twins (mate.twinChance), longer lives, a milder lean season; what the dead built stands empty and can be claimed by anyone, to begin a home or add to a band's; elders moved to hand on what only they know

[NOW] necessity as the mother of invention: what beings suffer (hunger, the lean season, cold, thirst, sickness, beasts, deaths, water they cannot cross, strife, storm, strange speech) sharpens them toward the ways that answer it; knowing neighbouring ways helps; you can set which hardships spur which way (op spur) and how strongly need counts (laws discovery.*)

[NOW] culture as something that can be read and followed: every tale, song, poem, myth, teaching, saying, lesson and way is an idea with an origin, holders and a path of spread; teachings that can be begun, heard, taken up and given up; talismans and carved figures; your statistics show which ideas are held most and which have crossed between peoples

[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value beyond the first talismans and carvings: special gems, named relics that gather a history; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed

[NOW] what is not forgotten: a blow or a theft that is seen leaves a grudge that holds a bond down until three gifts mend it or long time passes; a gift in need leaves a kindness that holds it up (laws culture.grudgeDays, kindDays, mendGifts); hunting together (fight.packBonus) and skill that grows with each hunt; telling by a fire, which makes tales; a roof that brings children sooner (mate.roofCooldown)

[NEXT] grudges from defeat or a stolen mate; compensation greater than gifts; peacemakers and peace ceremonies; hard feelings rarer inside a family or band than across them, and arising from conflict, wealth, history or charisma
[NEXT] rivalry for mates; heroes whose deeds spread as lore, to whom tribute is paid and whom the ambitious challenge; duels in which the winner takes most of what the loser holds
[NEXT] fighting, hunting and defending together as learned skills; calling for help and answering it
[NEXT] talents: skill in a way drawing one on along its line; learning what a way demands through dreams, visions from herbs or a shaman's prophecy, and quests to gather what it needs
[NEXT] bandits in new lands; stranger settlements friendly or hostile, with things to trade; farms and flocks as a settlement's steady food
[LATER] monsters that wander in rarely and can be killed only by a band together; their capture, taming and breeding from guarded eggs that others will try to steal
[NEXT] later callings that come with standing and ways: alchemists, scholars, scientists
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations, factories, plants that remake waste
[FAR] new materials far down the tree: plastics, silicon, rare earths
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.

The Kragrek lag behind. They are scattered, have no fire and no band, and all stand near or below the standing needed to lead. Kragog is parched and sick from raw meat in the Aeleth Sands. The peoples still have not met, and the lean season is at most a few days off.

Olum or Vorok should be measurably closer to fire, with more lore and some practice gathering wood and stone, and at least one Kragrek may come to fire before the cold sets in. The first lean season should pass with no deaths, and median energy should stay above 60.

from earlier worlds: Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

from earlier worlds: A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

from earlier worlds: Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

from earlier worlds: By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

from earlier worlds: Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

from earlier worlds: A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

from earlier worlds: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

from earlier worlds: Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

from earlier worlds: One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

from earlier worlds: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

from earlier worlds: Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

from earlier worlds: Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

from earlier worlds: A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

from earlier worlds: Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

from earlier worlds: A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

from earlier worlds: When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

from earlier worlds: Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

from earlier worlds: Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

from earlier worlds: A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

day 5: The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

day 9: A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

records.text: the Kragrek (Stone-folk) in the Halim Heights; the Pesi (Wood-folk) in the Vaeth Woods; the Phizhi (Canopy-folk) in the Ixra Rainforest: 3 peoples woke in different lands of a new world, a sea between them (seed 5614).
A stalker brought down a hopper.
Hanna found the grove "Kinmire".
Sevi found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Balar
records.text: Tugek! A dunecat prowls to the northeast. Come with me to the west, we are safer together. I am Balar.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: A dunecat four steps off, and it kills our kind; I will not stand here to be eaten. Tugek is near and strong, and I would rather have him between me and the cat, and later at my side. I move away from the cat toward the salt in the NW, and I will talk warmly to Tugek, since a man who follows me is worth more than one who fights me.
records.feeling: Dread of the dunecat, and a hungry eye on Tugek as a possible ally.

say.text: Tugek! A dunecat prowls to the northeast. Come with me to the west, we are safer together. I am Balar.

changes: set its aim: "Stay alive, win allies, and gather a following."
now wonders: What would make a strong man like Tugek follow me?

records.name: Brunde
records.text: I am Brunde of the Pesi. My fire is open to any who come. I go to gather flint to the northeast. Come with me if you wish.

records.name: Brunde
records.thought: I am fed and safe, and so my curiosity runs free. Flint and amber lie close to the northeast, and I have never taken anything from a deposit. I want to learn what they are for, and a hunter needs an edge on his hand. Hanna is a man alone nearby, and I'd rather make allies than stand apart, so I'll greet the others and then go gather.
records.feeling: Curious and hopeful about the stones to the northeast, and about the strangers near me.

say.text: I am Brunde of the Pesi. My fire is open to any who come. I go to gather flint to the northeast. Come with me if you wish.

changes: set its aim: "Become a skilled hunter and make allies who will share a fire with me"
now wonders: What can flint be made into, and who here would stand beside me?

records.name: Sevi
records.text: Pesi here! I am Sevi. No fire is left untended among my people, and none is refused a place at it. Come near, Nande, Hanna. Let us share what we know and find a fire together.

records.name: Sevi
records.thought: I want a fire that is mine too, and someone surer than me to stand behind. Hanna and Nande stand close and look strong, and none of us follows anyone yet. I'll go speak to them, offer them a place beside me, and see who is steady. Kinmire still hums in my mind, but people first.
records.feeling: Hungry for belonging, hopeful toward Nande and Hanna.

say.text: Pesi here! I am Sevi. No fire is left untended among my people, and none is refused a place at it. Come near, Nande, Hanna. Let us share what we know and find a fire together.

changes: set its aim: "Find a band to belong to and raise a shared fire and a hall with them"
now wonders: What is Kinmire, and does it want something from us?

records.text: Brunde won flint from the ground.

records.name: Tugek
records.text: I am Tugek. I hear your warning. I will go west with you, but I will watch the northeast as we go.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: Balar spoke to me first and offered company, and he is near, walking about. A dunecat to the northeast is a danger I cannot see, and I would rather leave before trouble finds me. I do not know him yet, but he named himself and gave a warning, and I want a place beside someone surer than I am. I will go west with him slowly and watch whether his word holds, and pick sunleaf on the way to taste it, since I have never eaten it.
records.feeling: Wary hope toward Balar, who offered company.

say.text: I am Tugek. I hear your warning. I will go west with you, but I will watch the northeast as we go.

changes: set its aim: "Find a band to belong to and learn how this world works."
now wonders: Is Balar's warning of the dunecat true, and can he be trusted?

records.name: Hanna
records.text: I am Hanna of the Pesi. I'll come to the flint. Keep fair and we'll deal fairly.

records.name: Hanna
records.thought: My belly is full and I have nothing to my name, no followers, no goods, no place. Brunde has gone for flint and offered his fire to anyone, and flint is something others will want, so I'll go there too and gather some. A merchant needs things worth trading, and I'll start with what's close: flint, then amber just beyond it. I'll watch how Brunde deals with me before I give him any trust.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with a wary curiosity toward Brunde.

say.text: I am Hanna of the Pesi. I'll come to the flint. Keep fair and we'll deal fairly.

changes: set its aim: "Become a trader of fine goods: gather flint and amber, and find who will deal for them."
now wonders: What do these people value enough to trade for?

records.text: A new wild plant appeared: nafrostcap (from frostcap).

records.name: Eltha
records.thought: A stalker sits five steps off and it kills my kind, so I will not linger here for it to pick me. I am fed, and I mean to be more than a woman who stands in the trees; I will be an explorer and be sung of. First I need stone and wood, so I will head north toward the flint, where the Pesi are gathering, and use their company as cover while I learn what the flint can give me.
records.feeling: Hungry for renown, and wary of the stalker to the southeast.
changes: set its aim: "Become a great explorer: gather flint and stone, make tools, then push past the edge of the known world."
now wonders: What lies beyond the edge of the known land, and who will follow me there?

records.name: Nande
records.text: I am Nande of the Pesi. I go to the edge of the world, northwest, to venture into the mist. Whoever wants to see new land first, come with me. I will keep a place at my fire for you when I return.

records.name: Nande
records.thought: Nine steps to the northwest the world simply stops, and no one has walked into that mist. I am bold and I am fed, so I mean to be the one who goes: land found first is remembered, and a name sung after me is the only thing that will outlast me. Sevi calls for a fire and Brunde digs flint, and I may come back and ask them to follow once I have something to show for it.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition, drawn toward the mist at the edge of the world.

say.text: I am Nande of the Pesi. I go to the edge of the world, northwest, to venture into the mist. Whoever wants to see new land first, come with me. I will keep a place at my fire for you when I return.

changes: set its aim: "Become a great explorer: be first to venture past the edge of the known world and find rich new land."
now wonders: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?

records.name: Balar
records.text: Good, Tugek. Stay close and I will see you fed. There is salt here, and I will gather it and share it with you.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The cat's dread still sits in my gut, but Tugek said he will go west with me, and that is the first thread of a following. A strong man follows one who gives him something, so I will give first and make him owe me. The salt is one step east, which is a first thing I can take, and I can make a sharing with Tugek near, so I will gather salt and then walk west with him.
records.feeling: Wary fear of the dunecat, and a hungry hope toward Tugek.

say.text: Good, Tugek. Stay close and I will see you fed. There is salt here, and I will gather it and share it with you.

records.text: Hanna won flint from the ground.

records.name: Brunde
records.text: Welcome, Hanna. The flint is plentiful, take what you need. I am going to taste the plainsroot. Stay and share the fire with me after.

records.name: Brunde
records.thought: I have flint in my hands and no notion yet what it is for, but I should learn it by using it. Hanna is coming to this stone, and he spoke fair, so I will stay near and let a bond grow rather than hurry off. The overwhelming itch is to taste the kelbulb and plainsroot, and they are only a few steps away, so I will harvest and eat a little to find out what they do to me.
records.feeling: Curious and warm toward Hanna, eager to taste the unknown plants.

say.text: Welcome, Hanna. The flint is plentiful, take what you need. I am going to taste the plainsroot. Stay and share the fire with me after.

records.text: Balar won salt from the ground.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: I woke among strangers, and one of them, Elyis, is standing right on top of me, which makes my skin prickle even though she has done nothing. I am fed and safe, so now I want to learn how this world works, and the flint to the west is the first thing I can reach that might become a tool. Gathering and testing will teach me more than waiting, and doing it near the others lets me watch who is steady enough to trust and perhaps follow.
records.feeling: Curious and a little wary of the strangers close around me.
changes: set its aim: "Learn how this world works by making tools from flint and stone, and find a steady person to stand with"
now wonders: What can flint and stone be made into, and which of these strangers can be trusted?

records.name: Kragog
records.text: I am Kragog. I mean to test what this ground gives. Will you walk with me and share what you learn?

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am fed and safe, yet I have no idea what I am for, and my curiosity burns. Vorok stands right beside me and Olum is close, both of my own kind, so I will not waste the chance to learn from them. Before I go looking for better ground, I want to taste the grain underfoot and try gathering stone from the rock nearby, because testing is how I learn how this world works.
records.feeling: Curious and restless, wanting to test things and find my purpose.

say.text: I am Kragog. I mean to test what this ground gives. Will you walk with me and share what you learn?

changes: set its aim: "Explore this land and learn how its stone, plants and peoples work, and find a place with water, food, wood and stone together."
now wonders: What can be made from the ore in this rock, and who among these strangers can be trusted?

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Greetings, Kragog, Olum. I am Vorok. This ground is poor, with water ten steps off and little wood. Shall we look for a better place together? I will share what I find and keep my word.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: Two of my own kind stand close, Kragog right beside me and Olum a few steps off, and my belonging aches to be near them. I am a talker and a sharer, so I will offer them a meal; sharing is how bonds begin, and I have nothing to hide. I want a fire and a place with water, wood and stone together, and I would rather search for it with others than alone.
records.feeling: A hungry wish to belong, turned toward Kragog and Olum.

say.text: Greetings, Kragog, Olum. I am Vorok. This ground is poor, with water ten steps off and little wood. Shall we look for a better place together? I will share what I find and keep my word.

changes: set its aim: "Find companions among my people and a good place to settle with them."
now wonders: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, and who will walk there with me?

records.text: Ssassa won flint from the ground.

records.name: Hanna
records.thought: Flint comes easily and I already hold five, but a merchant needs a second good and a buyer. Amber is two steps away, so I'll take some, then gather wood, which I've never done and which will help me build a place of my own. Brunde and Eltha stand close and seem fair. Everyone here is Pesi and has the same flint and amber, so my trade will have to be with other peoples, and I mean to find them.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with wary curiosity toward Brunde.
